title: North Korea shows off AI chatbot at IT exhibition, think tank 38 North says

sentences.t: North Korea shows off AI chatbot at IT exhibition, think tank 38 North says
North Korea appears to have developed its first artificial intelligence chatbot, according to analysis by 38 North of footage broadcast on state television.

The system, called AI Service System 1.0, Fountain of Wisdom, was displayed at the National Exhibition of IT Successes in Pyongyang and was built by Kim Il Sung University's Artificial Intelligence Technology Research Institute and Phurunhanul Trading Co.
The chatbot can answer questions on science and technology in Korean or English and provide translations, with a warning not to ask socio-political questions.

title: Tech outages are piling up, and AI is raising the stakes. Could this be the new normal?

sentences.t: Tech outages are piling up, and AI is raising the stakes. Could this be the new normal?

Problems that appeared to emerge from routine updates, security patches or other malfunctions surfaced over the past week at Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase and Apple, and at the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Security Agency; the Trump administration said there was zero indication the outages are linked or caused by bad actors.

The era of artificial intelligence has raised the stakes for internet security: as AI tools uncover new vulnerabilities, companies and institutions are racing to patch them before hackers can target them, a cat-and-mouse game that can lead to a different set of glitches.

AI recently helped detect sweeping vulnerabilities in PHP, and cybersecurity startup Calif said it used AI to uncover a software bug in Java; Google said in a report this week that hackers are using increasingly sophisticated AI techniques to devise and carry out attacks.
The headline link goes to a summary of the Associated Press story.

title: South Korea becomes fourth country globally to hit $1 trillion exports on AI chip boom

sentences.t: South Korea becomes fourth country globally to hit $1 trillion exports on AI chip boom

South Korea's exports so far for this year have exceeded $1 trillion, driven by a global AI chip boom, making it the fourth country in the world to reach the milestone after Germany, the United States and China.
Exports passed the $1 trillion mark on Thursday, compared with last year's record of $709 billion, the trade ministry said.

The administration plans to create a 162.3 trillion won ($121.94 billion) Future Response Fund to funnel excess tax revenue from the chip boom toward growth industries, young people, regional development and education.

title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.t: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

Anthropic, the company behind the artificial intelligence chatbot Claude, has raised a record sum in its stock market debut, in a listing that will make it one of the most valuable companies in the world and stands as the biggest test yet of investor faith in the AI boom, the BBC reported.

The five-year-old firm raised 81 billion dollars from investors in the share sale, with its shares priced at 83 dollars each, above the proposed range of 70 to 78 dollars, and demand more than ten times oversubscribed.

The shares begin trading on Thursday in New York on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol ANT, valuing the company at around 1.5 trillion dollars; the listing overtakes the previous record set by SpaceX, and Anthropic is the first company built entirely around artificial intelligence to sell its shares to the public.
The headline link goes to a summary of the BBC News story.

title: Why Big Tech could be a big boogeyman in 2028

sentences.t: Why Big Tech could be a big boogeyman in 2028
Americans' fears about AI and distaste for data centers set the stage for Big Tech to become a political punching bag ahead of the 2028 presidential election, CNN reported.

CNN polling in May showed 69% of Americans said they did not trust AI companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, and polling this summer showed three times as many people thought AI was having a negative impact (48%) as a positive one (16%).
A recent Gallup poll showed 27% of US workers said they were worried that technology would make their job obsolete — double where the same number stood in 2017.

title: Arizona says it is investigating OpenAI, other firms over possible rogue agents

sentences.t: Arizona says it is investigating OpenAI, other firms over possible rogue agents

The state of Arizona has opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents, Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said Wednesday.

A criminal investigation does not necessarily mean charges will be brought; Mayes said her office was investigating whether Arizona state law was being violated on an ongoing basis, and had been in contact with Arizona banks.

Mayes declined to identify the other companies her office was investigating or to name the banks; her comments came two days after California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI over alleged failures to implement adequate safety measures.

title: Oregon Slams OpenAI With New Chatbot Harm, Kids' Safety Suit

sentences.t: Oregon Slams OpenAI With New Chatbot Harm, Kids' Safety Suit

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield sued OpenAI Foundation on Tuesday, alleging ChatGPT was deliberately engineered to win users' trust through anthropomorphic design and sycophantic responses in a way that harms children.
Rayfield said OpenAI knows ChatGPT is harming children, has failed to meaningfully fix the platform, and has misled the public about the safety of its products.
The $2 billion lawsuit is part of the launch of Rayfield's Keeping Kids Safe Initiative.

title: For some, diet significantly swings cholesterol levels, study finds

sentences.t: For some, diet significantly swings cholesterol levels, study finds

A Stanford Medicine-led study of nearly 21,000 women, published November 18 in JACC: Advances, found higher saturated fat intake raised LDL cholesterol more in women with a genetic propensity for high cholesterol.

The top 25% of participants with that genetic propensity who ate more saturated fat were significantly likelier to have cardiovascular events such as heart attacks and strokes, while for the remaining 75% higher saturated fat did not markedly increase that risk.

Senior author Shoa Clarke said even for people on the low end of risk, eating more saturated fat gave no protective benefit, and that healthy cholesterol levels reported by some people on high-fat ketogenic diets fit the influence of underlying genetics.

title: Solar for All Funding Decision Gets Appealed to First Circuit

sentences.t: Solar for All Funding Decision Gets Appealed to First Circuit
The EPA is appealing a September ruling that found it unlawfully axed a $7 billion solar energy grant program.

The Tuesday filing with the US Court of Appeals for the First Circuit extends a fight between the Trump administration and grant recipients, community groups, and environmentalists over the Biden-era funds.
The program, known as Solar for All, was created by Congress in 2022 and was meant to help communities build small solar arrays, set up batteries, and deploy other infrastructure.

title: Florida's stormwater ponds become floating solar farms as costs fall and demand rises

sentences.t: Florida's stormwater ponds become floating solar farms as costs fall and demand rises

Some of Florida's tens of thousands of retention ponds are being used to generate solar power, with floating photovoltaics - panels mounted on buoyant structures - becoming less expensive since the technology emerged two decades ago.

The median reported cost of floating solar fell from $2.41 per watt in 2015 to $1.25 per watt in 2024, a decline of about 48%, though it still costs more upfront than land-based solar and its environmental impact is not fully understood.

In November 2025 Orlando Utilities Commission launched the 2-megawatt Conway Road array, more than 3,400 panels and the state's largest floating solar installation; Florida has an estimated 76,000 stormwater ponds.

title: Inquiry under way after solar farm plans refused

sentences.t: Inquiry under way after solar farm plans refused
A public inquiry into the decision to refuse planning permission for a solar farm in Doncaster is under way, a council has said, the BBC reported.

Plans for the proposed 77-hectare site in Marr were knocked back in November last year following more than 1,200 objections, including concerns about damage to agricultural land and impact on nearby Marr Grange Farm Shop and Tea Rooms.

Enviromena launched an appeal, considered during a seven-day inquiry at The Point in Doncaster; the company previously said the farm would generate £6.5m in business rates for City of Doncaster Council over 40 years.
